# Nirodhavāra (Ya 3.2.2)
**ID:** Ya 3.2.2
**Section:** Yamaka (ya)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 3.2.2) constitutes the second division of the *Pavattivāra* (the section on the process or occurrence of phenomena) within the *Saccayamaka* ("Pairs on the Truths"), the third chapter of the *Yamaka* in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Anderson 1999; SuttaCentral]. While the preceding section addresses origination (*uppādavāra*), the *Nirodhavāra* provides a systematic dialectical analysis of cessation, interrogating how each of the four noble truths ceases in relation to the others across the three temporal periods of past, present, and future, with respect to persons and planes of rebirth [Nyanatiloka 2007; Anderson 1999].
Scholars note that the *Yamaka*'s structural analysis of phenomena across the threefold scheme of origination (*uppādavāra*), cessation (*nirodhavāra*), and origination-cessation (*uppādanirodhavāra*) exemplifies early Buddhist process metaphysics, which interprets experience through transient processes rather than enduring substances [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. This analytical framework is functionally linked to the subdivision of a mental moment into distinct instants of arising (*uppādakkhaṇa*) and cessation or destruction (*bhaṅgakkhaṇa*), marking a pivotal stage in the doctrinal evolution toward a full theory of momentariness [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005].
SuttaCentral records one modern translation in one language and lists no direct historical parallels [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus reports widespread internal Pali text reuse (over 31,000 matches across 42 texts), consisting of shared structural and repetitive phrasing with counterpart sections of the *Yamaka*—most prominently its neighboring *Uppādavāra* (Ya 3.2.1) and *Uppādanirodhavāra* (Ya 3.2.3), as well as *Nirodhavāra* sections of other chapters (including Ya 5.2.2, Ya 9.2.2, and Ya 6.2.2) and commentary texts such as the *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments detected by DharmaNexus connect formulaic technical discussions with Sanskrit and Tibetan Abhidharma works, including the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā* (D4092) and the Sanskrit *Śrāvakabhūmi* of the *Yogācārabhūmi* [DharmaNexus].
